title: Inside The Navy's Indoor Ocean
beats: Navy wave pool: biggest in world, looks like an ocean; scale and 216 paddles
What makes it different is control: specific amplitude and frequency repeatably; 1 Hz demo
Waves transmit energy not matter; molecules go in circles, vanishing at half wavelength (wave base)
But ideal waves drift slightly: spiral path, faster at top
Same amplitude, three frequencies split-screen; steeper-looking, and slower for higher frequency
Dispersion demo: send high frequency first, low catch up and break at one spot
Quilt wave standing waves; bullseye wave focuses energy
Rubber duck drifts into breaking bullseye, swamped
Real purpose: scale ship models; 5 inch waves = 20 foot
Expected Reynolds number but waves scale by Froude number; speed 1/sqrt(46); slow footage by sqrt(46)=6.8
Five factors of wind wave size; swell is the low frequency survivors
Learner proposes concert bass analogy; expert confirms
Rogue waves are superposition, not out of nowhere
Wind waves in 3 steps to fully developed sea
Regular vs irregular waves: spectra differ by ocean (North Sea peaky, N Atlantic broad)
Ex-destroyer captain: mattress sliding; helicopter deck wetness test
RC boat flips in big waves
Carriage towed tests; tumblehome hull innovations

new_moves.name: instrument-controlled-demo
new_moves.what: Use a facility that varies one parameter at a time so each effect is isolated

new_moves.name: expectation-correction
new_moves.what: Host admits he expected a different rule (Reynolds) then reveals the actual one

new_moves.name: learner-offers-analogy
new_moves.what: Host proposes an analogy and checks it with the expert

theory: The video uses a facility with total control over waves as a physical simulation, varying one parameter at a time so each principle (dispersion, superposition, scaling) appears as a visible change. The host voices the expected wrong rule (Reynolds) and has it corrected on camera, which models honest expert learning.
velocity: Scene builder: a one-parameter-at-a-time slider scene with split-screen comparisons
Voice: say the expected-but-wrong rule aloud before the correct one
Orchestrator: after a demo, ask learner for an analogy and judge it, as at 11:00
Ghost hands: draw the circular particle path and fading depth before the wave runs
Evals: check that formulas appear only after a puzzle the learner has seen
